2027-04-25.title: Fourth Sunday after Qyomtho
readings: Go and make disciples of all nations
In a time of favour I have answered you
A new creation; ambassadors for Christ
You are witnesses of these things
2027-04-25.alt: Season of Qyomtho. In the 2025–26 lectionary this Sunday was Syro-Malankara Catholic Laity Day. Today is also the feast of St Mark the Evangelist.
2027-04-25.verse: And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
theo: The risen Lord stands among his frightened disciples: “Peace be with you… Why are you frightened, and why do doubts arise in your hearts? Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself.” He eats before them. Then “he opened their minds to understand the scriptures”: the Messiah had to suffer and rise, and “repentance and forgiveness of sins is to be proclaimed in his name to all nations… You are witnesses of these things.”

In the evening Gospel the risen Christ gives the great commission on a mountain in Galilee: “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything that I have commanded you. And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.” The Church exists to evangelise.

Peter discovers in the house of Cornelius that “God shows no partiality”: the Gospel is for every nation. St Paul calls every Christian an ambassador: “if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation… So we are ambassadors for Christ, since God is making his appeal through us.” This is why the Church honours the laity today: the mission is not only for priests and religious, but for every baptised person in family, work and society.

Job's fortunes were restored when he prayed for his friends; Solomon received wisdom when he asked for it. Let us ask the risen Lord for the wisdom and courage to be his witnesses, knowing that he is with us always.
conn: Isaiah 49:6, “a light to the nations”, is fulfilled when the risen Christ sends his disciples to all peoples (Luke 24:47; Matthew 28:19).
The risen body is real: hands, feet, eating fish (Luke 24:39–43). The Resurrection is not a vision.
2 Corinthians 5:17: in Christ the new creation begun on Easter morning reaches every believer.
Job 42:10: Job is restored when he prays for the friends who had wronged him.
altar: At the end of every Holy Qurbono the priest blesses and sends us out. That dismissal is the great commission: we leave the altar as witnesses, with the promise “I am with you always.”
outline: Touch and see; he eats with them.
Christ is the key to the Scriptures.
The great commission belongs to all the baptised: Laity Day.
Point 4 · I am with you always
live: Speak one word of faith or hope to a colleague or neighbour this week.
Offer your time to one parish ministry or lay association.
Pray for priests, sisters and lay missionaries from Kerala working in North India and abroad.
fathers: Christ showed them his wounds so that the marks of the nails and the spear might heal the wounds of unbelieving hearts (Sermon 73 on the Ascension, 2).
He did not say “I will be with you only”, but “with all who believe after you”; he spoke to all the faithful as to one body (Homilies on Matthew 90).
magis: The Christian vocation is by its nature a vocation to the apostolate; the laity share in the priestly, prophetic and kingly office of Christ.
The lay faithful are called to sanctify the world from within, in family, work and society.
The missionary mandate: the Church is sent to all nations.
saints: 25 Apr: St Mark the Evangelist. 29 Apr: St Catherine of Siena. 1 May: St Joseph the Worker. 2 May: St Athanasius of Alexandria.
2027-04-25.prayer: Risen Lord Jesus, you opened the minds of your disciples and sent them to all nations. Open our minds to the Scriptures, make us your ambassadors in our families and work, and keep us faithful to your promise: I am with you always. Amen.

quick: The risen Lord is real: “Touch me and see.”
“Go and make disciples of all nations”: every baptised person is sent.
“I am with you always, to the end of the age.”
2027-04-25.action: Speak one word of faith or hope to a colleague or neighbour this week.
2027-04-25.question: Where is the Lord sending me as his witness this week?
2027-04-25.special: Fourth Sunday after Qyomtho. Feast of St Mark. (In 2025–26 also Laity Day; check the collection.)
illus: A Kerala teacher in a government school never preached, but her honesty, patience and care for poor students made colleagues ask: “Why are you like this?” She answered simply: “Because of Jesus.” That is lay apostolate.

family.explain: Before going back to the Father, Jesus told his friends: “Go and tell everyone about me. I am with you always.” He says this to us too!
family.intention: We pray for missionaries and for courage to tell others about Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family show Jesus' love to our neighbours?”

catechism: The vocation of the lay faithful.
kidsaint: A Jesuit missionary who came to India and travelled along the coasts, baptising thousands and teaching children their prayers. He went as far as Japan. Lesson: Jesus sends each of us to share his love.
term: In the 2025–26 lectionary the Fourth Sunday after Qyomtho is Syro-Malankara Catholic Laity Day, when the Church prays for the lay faithful and supports their works.
termMore: Christ's last command in Matthew (28:18–20): go, make disciples, baptise, teach. It is the charter of the Church's mission.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the disciples are gathered, frightened and confused, when the risen Jesus stands among them: “Peace be with you. Why are you frightened? Look at my hands and my feet; it is I myself.” He even eats a piece of fish in front of them. The Resurrection is not a ghost story; the Lord is truly alive, body and soul.

Then he opens their minds to understand the Scriptures, and gives them a task: repentance and forgiveness of sins must be proclaimed in his name to all nations. “You are witnesses of these things.” In Matthew he says it on a mountain: “Go therefore and make disciples of all nations… And remember, I am with you always.”

This command is not only for priests and sisters. St Paul says every Christian is “an ambassador for Christ”. Today our Church honours the laity, because most of the world will never hear a sermon from a priest; they will only see Christ in you: in your honesty at work, your patience at home, your kindness to the poor, your courage to say “I am a Christian.”

Job was restored when he prayed for his friends. Solomon received wisdom when he asked. Let us ask the risen Lord for wisdom and courage, and go out from this Qurbono as his witnesses. He has promised: “I am with you always, to the end of the age.” Amen.
kids: Children, before Jesus went back to heaven, he gave his friends a big job: “Go and tell everyone about me!”
And he made a promise: “I will be with you always.” Jesus is with us every day, at school, at home, everywhere.
You can tell others about Jesus by being kind and honest. Let's say: “Jesus, I will be your helper!”

intro: The Risen Lord shows the disciples his hands and feet, opens their minds to the Scriptures, and sends them to all nations. The Gospel of this Sunday is the Church's charter of mission.

points.h: “Look at my hands”: a real, risen Lord
sub: The disciples are frightened and think they see a ghost.
Jesus shows his wounds: the Risen One is the Crucified One, truly alive in his body.
God never forgets us: our names are inscribed on the palms of his hands.
q: Can a woman forget her nursing child, or show no compassion for the child of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you. See, I have inscribed you on the palms of my hands.
He said to them, “Why are you frightened, and why do doubts arise in your hearts? Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself.”
points.apply: In moments of fear this week, look at a crucifix and remember: he has not forgotten you.

sub: God revealed himself to Moses as merciful and gracious.
Repentance and forgiveness are to be proclaimed in Christ's name to all nations.
Peter learns that God shows no partiality: every nation is welcome.
q: The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness.
Then Peter began to speak to them: “I truly understand that God shows no partiality, but in every nation anyone who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.”
points.apply: Reject every prejudice against people of other castes, languages or religions.

sub: God made his Servant a covenant for the people.
All authority is given to Jesus; he sends us to baptise and teach.
He does not send us alone: “I am with you always, to the end of the age.”
q: In a time of favor I have answered you, on a day of salvation I have helped you; I have kept you and given you as a covenant to the people.

Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything that I have commanded you. And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Support the missions with prayer and an offering; teach the faith to the children in your family.

concl: The Risen Christ shows his wounds, opens the Scriptures, forgives and sends.
Let us be his witnesses, confident that he is with us always.
2027-04-25.resolve: Pray for missionaries, especially those from Kerala serving in other lands.
